clue.text: Suitable travel make-up

parts.note: to travel is to go

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to make is to do, as in do a drawing

explanation.surface: A recommendation for cosmetics that hold up well on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics, but it splits into two jobs: a synonym of 'make' and 'up', which in a down clue turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suitable is fit for its purpose, as in a good time to call.

clue.text: Publicity she wrongly associated with Brummie's sticker

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of she are put in the wrong order

parts.note: Brummie is the setter, so Brummie's from the setter's own mouth is I've, 'I have'

explanation.surface: An advert that a woman wrongly linked to the setter's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for 'I', so 'Brummie's' read as 'Brummie has' becomes I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is anything that sticks, such as glue or tape.

clue.text: 'Ratio of a right angle bearing' — jargon!

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
cant is the special jargon of a group

explanation.surface: A mock complaint that trigonometry talk about ratios and bearings is mere jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry this is the ratio of hypotenuse to adjacent side for an angle of a right-angled triangle.

clue.text: Tabloid turned up with: 'Ron is terribly camp'

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: terribly means the letters of Ron is are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline quoting someone called Ron as dreadfully camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' looks like a description of Ron's manner; it is the definition, a military camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A military post or encampment manned by troops stationed there.

clue.text: 'King George', a soft old man's tipple

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
p, piano, is the musical mark for soft
pa, a father, is one's old man

explanation.surface: A soft old monarch's favourite drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink; this one is an Italian grape brandy.

clue.text: English writer makes US president (silly cow!) cross

parts.note: Gerald Ford was the 38th US president
mad means silly, crazy
an ox is a bovine animal, loosely a cow
to ford a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: An English novelist turns into an American leader, and an angry cow takes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly cow' reads as an insult but gives two pieces; 'cross' is not angry but a verb for wading a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist (1873-1939) who wrote The Good Soldier and Parade's End.

clue.text: Regular join should include one?

indicators.note: should include says the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: to solder is to join metal with molten alloy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question of whether a routine joint should contain a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, a professional member of the regular army.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a full-time professional serving member of a standing army.

clue.text: 'Rotting food swindle' admits épicier, finally, in the middle of Paris

indicators.note: admits says the con takes the rest in, around it

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: in says the grocer's last letter goes into the middle of the city name
the middle of means the letters of Paris without its first and last
finally picks the last letter of the word épicier

explanation.surface: A Parisian grocer's rotten produce is exposed as a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: ARI, the middle of Paris, takes in R, the end of épicier (French for grocer), giving ARRI, which CON then surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaying flesh of dead animals, food for scavengers such as vultures.

clue.text: Advantage of wife leaving club

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for wife departs from the club

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club

explanation.surface: A wife's gain in leaving her club, perhaps in a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a golf club, the wedge.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand over a rival, as in a slight lead over the field.

clue.text: Legendary ruler giving away universal ring case for scarab, say

indicators.note: giving away says the ruler loses the letter for universal

parts.note: King Arthur is the legendary ruler of Camelot
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
O is ring-shaped
a pod is the case holding seeds

explanation.surface: A mythical king gives up a universal ring kept in a case shaped like a beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab beetle is one example of the jointed-legged invertebrates that include insects and crabs.

clue.text: Fleeting romp turned into weeping

indicators.note: into says the jumbled romp goes inside the word for weeping

parts.note: teary means weeping

indicators.note: turned means the letters of romp are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A brief fling that ended in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: MPOR, the anagram of ROMP signalled by 'turned', goes into TEARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting only a short while, transient rather than permanent.

clue.text: Como is too wet in the middle!

indicators.note: in the middle says the letters sit inside the run of words Como is too

explanation.surface: A complaint that Lake Como is too rainy right at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' seems to describe the lake; it signals the letters hiding inside 'Como is too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp or slightly wet, as of a cake or soil.

clue.text: See 6
Conflict causes female to lose stone at first, getting lighter

indicators.note: lose says a letter is removed from the female title
at first says the letter goes from the front of its run

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried female
st or S is the abbreviation for the stone weight
a match is a lighter for a fire

explanation.surface: A slimming woman's struggle: losing weight early on and getting lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' looks like 'less heavy', the weight-loss story; it is something that lights, a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that clash or fail to go together, a poor pairing.

clue.text: Large asteroid sequence broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast says the word is spoken on air, so only its sound counts

parts.note: a series is a sequence

explanation.surface: A television series about a giant space rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest body in the asteroid belt, now classed as a dwarf planet.

clue.text: They have nothing to do with Eric introducing elements of a deal?

parts.note: Eric of Monty Python fame, whose surname means lazy
in a card game each player's set of cards is dealt as a hand

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who is unemployed when a Python comedian deals the cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric is the Monty Python comedian; 'introducing' places his surname before the cards. The phrase recalls 'the devil makes work for ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unoccupied workers are those with no job, nothing to do.

clue.text: Ex-PM, having been given a roasting?

definitions.meaning: meat that has been roasted turns this colour

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister who was savaged by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a roasting' suggests a fierce telling-off for the politician; here it is cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A former British premier's surname, and the colour food goes after roasting.

clue.text: Support (very Parisian) inserted in wobbly bust

indicators.note: inserted in says the French word goes inside the jumbled bust
wobbly says the letters of bust are shaken into a new order

parts.note: très is French, the Parisian's word, for very

explanation.surface: A French lingerie advert about supporting a wobbly bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inserted in' puts the French word inside BUTS, the rearrangement of 'bust' that 'wobbly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting structure that props up a wall, so a support.

clue.text: See 24
You wouldn't expect this bend on trip

parts.note: to wind is to bend and twist, as a road does
a fall is a trip, a stumble

explanation.surface: Warning that a sharp bend could cause an unexpected fall.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected gain, such as a sudden inheritance, is something nobody anticipated.

clue.text: Free entry of one into Grexit arrangement has advantage, initially

indicators.note: entry of says the letter for one joins the pool of letters from the other word
into names the word that the letter for one goes into before the shake-up
arrangement says the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a means one, as in a single item

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word advantage

explanation.surface: A Greek exit from the euro might be free to enter, with the first advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: Grexit was the proposed Greek exit from the eurozone. With A added, its letters rearrange to EXGRATI, and the first letter of 'advantage' ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'out of grace': given as a favour without legal obligation, so free.

clue.text: Dwelling briefly on final answer

parts.note: res is short for residence, a dwelling
ult is short for ultimate, final

explanation.surface: A quiz host pausing briefly before the contestant's final answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final answer' reads as one phrase, but 'final' gives ULT and 'answer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The outcome of a sum or calculation is its solution.

clue.text: See 15
Worn inside the woman's waders

indicators.note: inside says the first piece sits within the woman's word

parts.note: hers means belonging to the woman
clothes worn are on

explanation.surface: A woman's waterproof waders, with something worn inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waders' looks like fishing boots; here they are wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged wading birds that fish in shallow water.

clue.text: No builder's storeyed construction should be by river

indicators.note: construction says the letters of storeyed are built into a new order

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A building regulation: a multi-storey block should sit beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No builder' is the definition: something that wrecks rather than builds.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecker is the opposite of someone who builds things.

clue.text: Writer's pulse

definitions.meaning: Roald, author of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
a pulse is an edible seed such as a lentil, here split peas also spelt dal

explanation.surface: An author's heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's author's surname, and a spelling of the Indian lentil dish.

clue.text: See 6
Peel, elected after resistance, died

indicators.note: after says the elected word and the died letter come behind the resistance letter

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
a party elected is in

explanation.surface: A Victorian obituary: Peel, elected after facing resistance, has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' looks like Sir Robert Peel, the Prime Minister; it is the skin of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer skin of fruit such as an orange.

clue.text: A consummate example — end of argument!

definitions.meaning: the phrase followed by 'in' means the ultimate example, as in the latest in fashion
having the final say ends a dispute

explanation.surface: A boast that one's point is unbeatable, closing the debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the supreme example of something, and the closing remark that settles a dispute.

clue.text: No good entering antelope country

indicators.note: entering says the no-good letters go inside the antelope

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: No good comes of an antelope entering farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like countryside; it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation of the United Kingdom, south of Scotland.
